Story & Plot

The RajaSaab follows a young man seeking his lost grandfather or doting grandmother's lost reputation who enters a haunted mansion and awakens a powerful family curse. The 186-minute Indian fantasy horror comedy mixes a coming-of-age narrative with a motley-crew comedy inside a haunted palace, a rom-com, a magical adventure, and a mystical thriller. Directed by Maruthi Dasari, the film combines mass elements with a series of ideas loosely tied together.

Comedy & Entertainment

The film attempts a horror-comedy tone with a motley-crew comedy set inside a haunted palace alongside ridiculous yet fun contrivances. However, the humor faces criticism from reviewers who note stale humour and an unintended labyrinth of scattered ideas. The lighter moments struggle to maintain a consistent comedic rhythm throughout the lengthy runtime.

Performances & Direction

The film features an ensemble cast including Prabhas, Sanjay Dutt, Zarina Wahab, Nidhhi Agerwal, and Malavika Mohanan. Reviewers note that an affable Prabhas does his best with the material, though his presence occasionally gets lost in a giant, spiraling mess. The performances are weighed down by a confused script that struggles to give the actors cohesive material to work with.

Strengths

  • Affable presence of Prabhas
  • Ambitious fantasy and horror-comedy premise
  • Motley-crew setup inside a haunted palace
  • Mass elements and bold ideas

Weaknesses

The film suffers from a thin plot, stale humour, and uneven execution that makes it feel like an unintended labyrinth. Clocking in at nearly three hours, the first half takes its time to establish the world with far too many songs, slowing the pace and causing the film to stretch and lose momentum. The writing lacks cohesion, and the storytelling struggles with a screenplay that feels like a series of ideas loosely tied together.

Final verdict

The RajaSaab is a missed opportunity that buckles under its own weight and a confused, overlong narrative. While it features an affable lead and an intriguing fantasy-horror setup, the lack of narrative focus makes it a tough recommendation. Viewers looking for a tightly wound horror-comedy may want to skip this exhausting and sprawling experiment.
